item: Wikipedia, ORES and DuckDuckGo sessions refuse a redirect to a host outside their list, on every hop
key_paths: src/safety/fetcher.py; src/wiki/client.py; src/wiki/ores.py; src/services/duckduckgo.py; tests/test_session_host_list.py; docs/SECURITY.md
summary: The parked LOW from the sink sweep: the three clients followed any redirect from their fixed endpoints with no host check and no connect-time SSRF guard. requests calls Session.send for the first request and again for every hop, and GuardedSession only overrode request, so the app-level kill-switch refusal and the transport decision ran on the first URL only (requests carries the proxy mapping onto hops and the airplane socket guard stands under both; no check looked at where a hop went). GuardedSession now takes an optional allowed_hosts and checks the whole URL in send, before every request: EthicalFetcher._refuse_parser_mismatch (backslash, whitespace or control in the authority, any percent in the host, the two parsers disagreeing, non-IDNA hosts), then https only, no userinfo, port 443 only, and a listed host (an exact host, or a leading-dot suffix meaning any host under it, never the bare domain or an empty label), each checked against both readings of the URL (urllib3's and urlparse's; requests 2.32.2 and later connects to the latter). A refusal is RedirectRefused, a RequestException and not a ConnectionError, raised before the request is sent, naming the clause and never the address. Lists: the wiki client wikimedia.org + .wikimedia.org + .wikipedia.org (its one shared session also serves pageviews on the bare apex and EventStreams), ORES .wikimedia.org, DuckDuckGo duckduckgo.com + .duckduckgo.com. Every other session stays unlisted and is pinned in UNLISTED_SESSIONS with zero slack and a reason per row: bulk downloads, the installer and the statistics catalogue (request-chosen hosts), and six fixed API endpoints (five Wikidata loaders and the Hugging Face release check; listed since, in PR #1394). List entries must be names of two or more labels; walk.refusal_token names a RedirectRefused request_refused, not connection_failed. Tests: each refusal clause has a test only it can fail, and a mutation matrix (scratch script, not committed) over the check left no survivor. One independent read: 0 block, 2 should-fix, 9 low, folded. Not covered, and said so: the unlisted sessions; no connect-time SSRF scope (the hosts are fixed public ones). Ruff advisory 417 of 417.
